peer_results.rationale: BAC's candidate disclosures relate to the adoption of amended segment reporting requirements (ASU 2014-08) and accounting for interest income on debt securities. Neither topic is substantively comparable to JPM's adoption of ASU No. 2023-02 regarding the proportional amortization method for investments in tax credit structures.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU No. 2023-02 for Tax Credit Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, allowing the use of the proportional amortization method for certain tax-incentivized investments, which had no material impact on the financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citi adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, allowing the use of the proportional amortization method for investments in tax credit structures. A key difference is the reported financial impact: JPM's adoption resulted in a decrease to retained earnings (implied by the alignment context mentioning a decrease to retained earnings for alternative energy investments), whereas Citi explicitly stated that the adoption did not have a material impact on its financial statements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-02 on Proportional Amortization for Tax Credits
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2024, the firm adopted ASU No. 2023-02 under a modified retrospective approach, expanding the proportional amortization method election to additional qualifying tax credits and requiring incremental disclosures; adoption had no material impact.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Goldman Sachs adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 2024 using the modified retrospective approach to expand the proportional amortization method for tax credits. Both firms reported that the adoption of this new accounting guidance did not have a material impact on their consolidated financial statements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of Proportional Amortization Method for Tax Equity Investments
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm adopted the accounting update for Investments - Equity Method and Joint Ventures - Tax Credit Structures on January 1, 2024, using the modified retrospective method, which permits electing the proportional amortization method for tax equity investments meeting certain conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Morgan Stanley adopted the accounting update for Investments in Tax Credit Structures effective January 1, 2024, using the modified retrospective method. Both firms elected to apply the proportional amortization method to eligible tax equity investments, specifically noting renewable energy and other tax equity programs. The alignment context for MS indicates a $60 million net-of-tax decrease to Retained earnings from this adoption, while JPM's context also notes a decrease to retained earnings, though specific dollar amounts vary.
